title: White-label partners for agencies: what to look for
author: Renee Editorial
summary: A white-label partner creates capacity without you having to hire. What matters are clear agreements on confidentiality, rights and data protection. A small test job shows more than any portfolio.

p: White label fits when workload fluctuates or individual disciplines such as 3D are missing. Your agency stays responsible for strategy and the client relationship; production sits with the partner.

list: Confidentiality: NDA before the first briefing
Usage rights: full transfer to the agency
Liability and how errors are handled

p: As soon as personal data is involved, you need a data processing agreement. If the partner is based in a country without a recognised adequate level of data protection, standard contractual clauses are usually added. Clarify this before client data starts to flow, and pass on only what the task requires.

Assign a real, small task with a normal briefing. Look at three things: the questions they ask, whether they meet the deadline and how many corrections are needed. The result shows what collaboration will look like under time pressure.
